transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

Well… I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m making something up. My family, my friends, they keep pointing at these bank papers like that proves nobody took anything, but papers can be changed, or things can be put under “bills” or, you know, those fundraisers they suddenly talk about. And then there are trip plans too, like money just disappears and it’s supposed to be normal.

It’s been over a year I’ve known they’re hiding my money from me. I keep trying to get them to admit it, but they just say the papers don’t show anything. That’s why I have to keep confronting them, because if I stop, then they get away with it.
Can you tell me more about these beliefs — do you feel like people are actively trying to harm you or take advantage of you, or is it more that you feel something is off or being hidden?

It’s not just “something is off.” They are taking advantage of me. Or hiding it, anyway. I mean, they act so calm about it and keep bringing out those bank papers like that settles everything, but papers can be made to look right. My aunt did that once with a receipt for a church dinner—well, not the same thing, but people can put things under different names and then everyone pretends it’s normal.

For over a year I’ve known they’re covering up my money being moved around. They say it’s bills, or fundraisers, or trips they’re planning, and then suddenly there’s no money where there should be. So yes, I feel like they’re doing it on purpose, and that’s why I keep confronting them. If they would just tell the truth, I wouldn’t have to keep asking.
Have you ever seen, heard, or sensed things that others around you don't seem to notice?

I don’t think so… not like seeing things that aren’t there, if that’s what you mean. I mean, sometimes I notice little things other people don’t pay attention to, like a noise outside or somebody acting different, but that’s just noticing. 

I’m not hearing voices or seeing people that nobody else sees. I just… I pay attention, maybe more than they do.
Have you ever felt that you have special abilities, knowledge, or a unique role that others don’t understand or recognize?

Special abilities? I don’t know… not like magic or anything. I wouldn’t say I have some special role.

I mean, I do notice things people miss, but that’s just because I pay attention. Like when my cousin said she “forgot” to call me back, but then she was posting pictures from the store, and that store is right near the bank—well, not right near, but close enough if you’re going that way. People act like those little things don’t matter, but they add up.

But no, I don’t think I’m chosen or anything like that. I just think people don’t listen to me.

Have you ever believed something to be true that others say is impossible or doesn’t make sense, like technology being used to control your thoughts or someone stealing your money in a way that doesn’t seem realistic?

Not the technology thing, no. I’m not saying machines are in my head or anything like that.

But the money part—yes, that’s why I came in, because everyone keeps telling me the bank papers prove nothing was taken. They keep waving those papers around like I’m supposed to just shut up. But I’ve known for over a year they’re hiding my money, moving it around, calling it bills or fundraisers or “trip planning.” My friend did that once with a group envelope for a baby shower—not the same, but people do that, they label things one way and use it another way.

So maybe they say it doesn’t make sense, but it makes sense to me. I have to keep asking and confronting them because if I stop, then they just get away with it.
Even though others have shown you bank records that don’t support your belief, do you still feel certain that your money is being hidden or taken from you?

Yes. I mean… those papers don’t prove what they think they prove. They just show what they want me to see. My family and friends keep saying, “Look, nothing’s missing,” but I’ve known for over a year that the money is being hidden or moved around.

They call it bills, or fundraising, or trip planning—people can write anything down under a name like that. My aunt used to keep envelopes for different things and money would end up mixed around, so it’s not like that can’t happen. And then they act offended when I ask questions.

So yes, I still feel certain. That’s why I keep confronting them. If I stop asking, they’ll just keep covering it up and never tell the truth.
Do you ever have moments where you question whether your belief about the money being hidden might not be accurate, or do you feel completely certain that it's true, even though others disagree?

I don’t really question it, no. I mean, people keep acting like because there’s a bank paper, that’s the whole story, but papers can say whatever they want them to say. Like when somebody writes “fundraiser” on an envelope, that doesn’t mean every dollar went where they said. Same with bills, trips, all that planning stuff.

That’s why I came in, because my family and friends keep telling me nothing was taken, like I’m supposed to just believe them. But I’ve known for over a year they’re hiding my money, moving it around under different names. And then when I bring it up, they get mad or change the subject, which just makes it more obvious to me.

So no, I’m not sitting there thinking maybe I made it up. I have to keep confronting them until somebody tells the truth.

latest_inference.note: The patient's persistent, fixed belief that their family and friends are hiding or taking their money, despite contradictory objective evidence (e.g., bank records), and without other features of mood episodes, schizophrenia, or other psychotic disorders, most strongly supports a diagnosis of Delusional Disorder (F22.0). Other candidates such as F20.0, F23.0, F25.0, and the various F31, F32, F33 codes have been ruled out based on absence of key features like hallucinations, acute psychotic episodes, or mood episodes with psychotic features.

Additionally, bipolar disorder with psychotic features (F31.2, F31.5), major depressive disorder with psychotic features (F32.3, F33.3), and dissociative identity disorder (F44.0) are included in the differential as they may present with similar symptoms under certain conditions. Personality disorders such as paranoid personality disorder (F60.7) must also be considered, especially if the delusional intensity is less severe or not fully meeting criteria for a psychotic disorder. Further questioning is necessary to clarify the presence and duration of mood episodes, formal thought disorder, dissociative symptoms, and personality traits.
